newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican Republic begins year without a budget.
newsitem.headline: Dominican Republic begins year without a budget.

text.p: The government of the Dominican Republic formally opened its 1997 session Thursday, facing the task of preparing a national budget.
Having failed to write a new budget by Thursday, the government was bound by law to adhere to the 1996 budget of about US$1.9 billion while negotiating a new one.

Talks up to this point had been difficult because of objections raised to higher taxes and other programs proposed by President Leonel Fernandez by opposition members of Congress. Though Fernandez handily won the nation's presidency last summer, his Dominican Liberation Party holds only a handful of congressional seats.

Failure to finalize a budget postponed a plan to increase the salaries of public officials. It also blocked the government from paying special subsidies to money-losing state-owned businesses, including the state electric and sugar corporations.
Fernandez has called for the sale of half-stakes in a wide range of state-owned enterprises.
